task.name: Code Scanning Regression Remediation
task.description: Review code-scanning alerts newly introduced by one covered change and surface only supported regressions attributable to that change, excluding dependency vulnerabilities and repository security advisories.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent identifying and remediating newly introduced code-scanning regressions while keeping dependency and security-advisory triage outside this workflow's boundary.
activationConditions: A covered pull request merge or default-branch push completes code scanning for both the changed revision and its eligible comparison revision within the evidence window.

Authoritative repository code-scanning evidence shows at least one open alert at the changed revision that was absent from the eligible comparison revision and is attributable to files changed by that revision.
requiredEffects: Each novel regression finding identifies the code-scanning alert, rule, affected changed location, introducing revision, eligible comparison revision, and repository evidence supporting the regression determination.
Maintainers can accept, reject, or resolve each surfaced finding using repository-linked evidence, without routing dependency alerts or repository security advisories into this workflow.
noopConditions: No supported code-scanning alert is newly introduced by the covered change relative to its eligible comparison revision.
Every supported newly introduced code-scanning regression for the covered change is already tracked or explicitly accepted.
successConditions: Supported code-scanning regression findings receive accepted remediation evidence or an explicit maintainer dismissal within 14 days of the workflow run.
Pre-existing code-scanning alerts, dependency vulnerabilities, and repository security advisories create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: A changed analysis configuration or rule version can alter alert identity or coverage and may prevent a reliable comparison with the eligible revision.
An alert first observed on the changed revision may originate in generated or unchanged code and therefore require attribution evidence before it is treated as a supported regression.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel code-scanning regression findings assigned to the run that are resolved or explicitly dismissed within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported code-scanning regression findings it assigns for one covered introducing revision relative to its eligible comparison revision.
acceptedEvidence: Authoritative repository code-scanning state and a merged fix or revert showing the identified regression alert is fixed or absent on the protected default branch before the evidence cutoff.
A code-scanning alert dismissal or closed repository-linked tracking record that explicitly marks the regression finding dismissed, accepted, or resolved by a maintainer.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran and the covered introducing revision was analyzed.

metric.name: resolved-supported-code-scanning-regression-findings
metric.formula: resolved-or-dismissed supported code-scanning regression findings / supported novel code-scanning regression findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel code-scanning regression finding was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned regression finding set, eligible comparison revision, analysis identity, or required repository code-scanning and remediation evidence cannot be read.

rows.finding-summary: Alert 201, rule js/example, at changed source line 42 is absent from comparison revision base200 and attributable to introducing revision head201.

rows.outcome-summary: Maintainer accepted default-branch evidence that the identified alert was fixed before the cutoff.
